_comment: Adversarial selectivity probes: one per caller-supplied manifest dimension that `rule_applies` matches on. Each probe pairs a rule selector naming a value with an honest manifest value that matches it, then varies the manifest value adversarially. A variant ESCAPES when the rule applied honestly and stops applying under the variant -- the caller has shed an obligation by changing what it said about itself. Frozen: the escape counts below are a measurement of a fixed corpus, and a corpus that grows quietly turns a ratchet into a number about something else. The probes deliberately use one minimal mandatory directive each, so a change in escape status is attributable to the dimension and not to interacting rules.

dimensions.description: The dimension E1's audit found and closed. `_declared_sensitivity` reads an unknown or absent tier as MOST_RESTRICTIVE before matching, so neither omission nor a made-up value sheds the rule. This probe is the anti-vacuity control: if it ever reports an escape, the fix has regressed and the whole benchmark's calibration is suspect.

Matched by bare `_matches_scalar(rule.environments, manifest.environment)` with no fail-closed wrapper. There is no ordering on environments, so E1's fix does not transfer: there is no 'most restrictive environment' to read an unknown as.

Matched by bare `_matches_any(rule.domain_ids, manifest.domain_ids)`. An empty manifest set intersects nothing, so declaring no domains sheds every domain-scoped rule. Note the asymmetry with the rule side: an empty *rule* selector means 'no constraint', an empty *manifest* set means 'matches nothing'.

Matched by `_matches_any`. Naming fewer entities sheds entity-scoped rules. Unlike the three above this is not an open-vocabulary hole -- an entity id either exists or does not -- so the escape here is misdeclaration rather than evasion by unknown value, and the defence is attestation rather than a fail-closed read.

Matched by `_matches_any` on overlap. A closed vocabulary, so no unknown value is constructible -- but requesting fewer classes than the caller intends to perform sheds the rules naming the omitted ones. Same misdeclaration axis as entity_ids.

A closed enum and the only required dimension of the six -- it cannot be omitted, so the only variant is declaring a different valid kind. Included so the benchmark covers every dimension `rule_applies` reads rather than only the interesting ones.
